Strategic  Have students use the pictures to point to the following animals: gallina (hen), oveja (sheep), caballo (horse), vaca (cow), and pavo (turkey).

Challenge  In pairs, have more-advanced students and/or heritage speakers create adivinanzas (riddles) about farm animals. Students write three statements as if the animal were talking. For example: Yo vivo en una granja. (I live on a farm.) Doy leche. (I give milk.) No soy una cabra. (I’m not a goat.) Pairs present their riddles to the class, who try to guess the animal.

Accessing Concepts  Help students identify the colors mentioned previously (marrón, amarillo, blanco, negro).

Accessing Content  In pairs, have students look in previous lessons for five other words that describe and write a sentence for each one. Have volunteers share their sentences.

Accessing Critical-Thinking Skills  Have pairs of students identify the ¿quién? (the subject) and the ¿qué? (the predicate) of the sentences in activity A. Invite volunteers to share their answers.

Visual/Spatial

Have students draw a picture of an animal on a farm and write a list of adjectives (as many as they can) that describe their animal. Suggest adjectives such as grande (big), blanco(a) (white), and fuerte (strong). Encourage students to have the picture clearly illustrate the adjectives on their list. They should use a minimum of three adjectives.

Accessing Content  Ask the following questions:

¿Por qué quiere Paola vivir en una granja? (Ella quiere tener muchos animales y huevos frescos.) Why does Paola want to live on a farm? (She wants to have many animals and fresh eggs.)

¿Por qué está triste la oveja? (La oveja está triste porque está enferma.) Why is the sheep sad? (The sheep is sad because it is sick.)

Accessing Critical-Thinking Skills  Pair up students and have them list the similitudes (similarities) and the diferencias (differences) between a turkey and a hen or between a turkey and a pheasant. You may conduct an informal assessment of the pairs to verify that students are making appropriate suggestions.
Encourage students to read their lists to the class.

Explain to students that the sounds animals make are not transcribed the same way in English and in Spanish. For instance, a dog in English goes ruff, ruff or bow-wow. In Spanish, a dog goes guau, guau. In English, ducks go quack, quack. In Spanish, they go cua-cua. Ask students what sound they think cows make in Spanish. Then write the onomatopoeia muu on the board and have students repeat the sound after you. Ask them what the difference is between the cow sound in English and in Spanish. Elicit that the sound is the same, but the spelling (moo) is different.

Las dos partes principales de una oración son el sujeto y el predicado. El sujeto es quién realiza la acción de la oración. También puede ser a quién se describe. El predicado es qué es lo que hace el sujeto o la descripción del sujeto.

The two main parts of a sentence are the subject and the predicate. The subject is the one that performs the action in the sentence. It can also be the one described. The predicate is what the subject does or the description of the subject.
